# s465ba (round 23, task #1028, edited ROW BY ROW): bop.t 253/256 -> 480/29.
#   ONE cause -- the bitwise `& | ^ ~` mode decision sent every non-string
#   operand (a ref, glob, qr//, blessed object, undef) to the NUMERIC op where
#   perl STRINGIFIES it and does the bit-string op, so `undef | "abc"` was 0
#   and `[1] | "\0"x40` was 1.  224 blessed fail rows left fail-baseline.tsv by
#   EDIT (join key = sweep-diff's file+description; the 15 that remain are the
#   14 named rows still failing plus the ONE key every unnamed row collapses
#   onto -- see #1041).  The 7 error-half rows are the over-0xFF fatal, now
#   raised with perl's own wording.  bop.t stays PARTIAL (509 of 510 rows;
#   the last row is the pre-existing `formline` child-program drop).
# s463au (round 20, edited ROW BY ROW): substr.t 348/2 -> 351/0.  ONE row again,
#   THREE test rows, all task #960 half (b) — substr/vec/pos take their TARGET
#   ARGUMENT in perl's loose lvalue context, so the `=` and 4-argument write
#   spellings reach a PLACE the way #939 made the `=~` spelling reach one.
#     351  `substr($#ta,0,2) = 23`     was -1, want 23 (a blessed-free NEW fail
#     353  `substr($#ta,0,2,23)`        above the abort point, so it read as
#                                       UNSTABLE, never as a baseline row)
#     142  `substr($data{a},0,5,"")` on a TIED hash element — a REGISTERED SKIP
#          that now passes, found by the registry's own stale-detector
#          (`# REGISTRY-STALE: substr.t test 142 now passes`) and dropped from
#          cl/skip-registry.lisp in the same commit.  Its registration blamed
#          tie write-through; the cause was the RAW ELEMENT (s455), so the 4-arg
#          call got the element's value and p-substr's write is silent on a
#          non-box.  With the element's BOX it is the box holding the tie proxy,
#          and box-set has always run STORE through one.
#   Attributed on the 6e6f191 base with a SERIAL single-file run of the same
#   file: base 348/2, this tree 351/0, both aborting after test 353, and the
#   whole TAP diff between the two trees is those three rows.  fail-baseline is
#   UNCHANGED — substr.t's one blessed row is test 372, above the abort point.
# s462at (round 19, edited ROW BY ROW): substr.t 347/3 -> 348/2.  ONE row, the
#   `is $#ta, 23` at t/op/substr.t:893 whose statement is
#   `substr($#ta, 0, 2) =~ s/\A..\z/23/s;`.  #939: an lvalue substr used as an
#   `=~` TARGET now binds the write-through cell (p-substr-lvalue-cell), and
#   substr's own target argument is a place too, so `$#ta` becomes
#   p-arylen-lvalue-cell and the substitution resizes @ta as perl does.  It was
#   -1 before (the substitution ran against a raw CL string and #911 turned that
#   into a read-only death, which aborted the top-level form).
#   Attributed on a 4c354bc worktree with a SERIAL single-file run of the same
#   file: base 347/1 aborting after test 351, this tree 348/2 aborting after
#   353.  So the fix both PASSED its own row and unblocked the next two, one of
#   which (`substr($#ta,0,2,23)` -- the 4-arg spelling of the same write) fails
#   HONESTLY and is task #960.  The remaining rows of the block need `sub
#   :lvalue`, which PCL drops loudly; the parallel run this baseline is taken
#   from produces the same 350 rows as before with one fail turned pass.
# s460ap (round 17, edited ROW BY ROW): multideref.t 42/10 -> 43/9.  ONE row,

#   RHS snapshot kept the LIVE box for a reference, so store 1 read $x->{a}

#   in the same run (REGISTRY-STALE: undef.t test 17 now passes) and the registry
#   entry was removed in the same commit, per the stale-detector rule.  Its
#   neighbours 16 (`undef $1` -- the undef BUILTIN, not a #873 write slot) and 18
#   (`undef &constant_sub`) still skip.

# s435 (THE FLIP — Option B phase 2's last step; ruled fable-answers-s433.md
#   §A.1, accept-the-price ruled in the s435 review): a statement the compiler
#   cannot lower is no longer replaced by `nil` with the program running on —
#   it is replaced by a `p-die`, so reaching it dies, perl-shaped and trappable.
#   FOUR files lost rows, all EDITED BY HAND, none re-blessed.  TOTAL passing
#   18366 -> 18311 (-55).  THE COST MODEL, recorded because it is what a future
#   session will want: the unit of the DECISION is the STATEMENT, but the unit
#   of the LOSS is the enclosing TOP-LEVEL FORM.  (perl's own loss unit for an
#   untrapped run-time die is the whole remaining program; the sweep's
#   p-load-with-recovery, #467, already narrows that to the one form — so PCL
#   post-flip loses LESS than perl would given the same program.)  The lost
#   rows are not a debt written off: each names a census owner below, and the
#   rows return when that gap closes.
#   substr.t 375 -> 347, status OK -> PARTIAL (ran 353 of 397).  Two drops,
#     both the lvalue-sub refusal (`bar = "XXX"` substr.t:697 and
#     `ta_tindex() = 23` substr.t:900) — census family 1, a REGISTERED absence
#     (not-supported.md §Lvalue subroutines), no owner task because it is
#     deliberate.  Drop 1 sits in a 190-line top-level form with 18 later
#     test-calls in a loop, drop 2 in the file's last form with 4.  The old
#     "OK" was a false OK — a file reported complete while missing two
#     statements; PARTIAL is the honest status and the honest fix target.
#   method.t 97 -> 72 (ran 124 of 163).  ONE drop — `is((method $obj "a","b",
#     "c"), …)` at method.t:72, the indirect-object family, census family 10,
#     owner **#399**.  It sits inside the top-level `(let (($obj …)) (let
#     (($mname …)) …))` that a file-level `my` wraps around the whole rest of
#     the file, so one drop costs 39 unrun rows.  This is the multiplier the
#     ruling did not have: a file whose loss is out of proportion PROMOTES its
#     drop's owner task, it does not bend the flip.
#   split.t 178 -> 177 and bop.t 253 -> 252.  Both are the ACCIDENTAL-PASS kind
#     and both are IMPROVEMENTS: a `fresh_perl_is(…, '')` whose child program's
#     only statement is a drop.  The child used to print nothing, so the row
#     matched '' and passed while testing nothing; the child now dies, so the
#     row fails honestly and joins fail-baseline.tsv.  split.t:682 "scalar
#     split stack overflow" (child `split//.0>60for"0000…"`); bop.t:701
#     "[perl #17844] access beyond end of block" (child `formline X000n…`,
#     the registered §format/write absence).  Attributed on a HEAD worktree,
#     and each child probed alone vs perl — bop.t's other two children are
#     unaffected.  NOTE: these two are the sixth population — a drop inside a
#     fresh_perl/runperl CHILD is invisible to the drop census, which reads
#     emitted .lisp files (task #472).
# s440 (agent s441c, task #468 -- a NEVER-declared sub call reaches the package's
#   AUTOLOAD, through the ONE %p-call-of-undefined-sub mechanism re-entered at
#   the call by encapsulating SBCL's restart-undefined): sort.t 203 -> 204 and
#   1 -> 0 fails, EDITED BY HAND.  The row is sort.t 177 "AUTOLOAD without stub"
#   (`sort.t:880`-ish: a comparator NAME with no body in a package with an
#   AUTOLOAD), which the fail baseline carried since its first bless and which
#   left that file by EDIT in the same commit.  The ONLY mover of the interim
#   s440 sweep (TOTAL 18312 -> 18313, GATE clean, 0 new, drops 5 = census).
# s436 (#456 half (b) / #469, the PHASE MODEL): sort.t 202 -> 203 and PARTIAL ->
#   OK, EDITED BY HAND — the row the s432 note below promised back.  PCL now
#   emits every section's COMPILE phase (defs, BEGINs) before any section's RUN
#   phase, as perl does, so `package A; sub min` is defined before the earlier
#   block's `sort { A::min(@$a) <=> A::min(@$b) }` runs: the comparator calls
#   the real sub, the list sorts, and `cmp_ok($answer,'eq','good','bug 36430')`
#   passes for the reason the test intends.  The file also stops aborting a
#   top-level form, hence OK.  It is the ONLY row the phase model moved in this
#   population (sweep TOTAL 18311 -> 18312, GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed).
# s432 (#456 half (a), the forward-declaration stub): sort.t 203 -> 202 EDITED BY
#   HAND, and its status OK -> PARTIAL.  The lost row is `cmp_ok($answer,'eq',
#   'good','bug 36430')` (sort.t:870), which was an ACCIDENTAL pass: the block's
#   `sort { A::min(@$a) <=> A::min(@$b) }` runs BEFORE the `package A; sub min`
#   that follows it in the same block (PCL emits the package switch as its own
#   section), so both calls reached the forward-declaration STUB.  The stub
#   answered nil, undef <=> undef is 0, the list came back unsorted, $answer was
#   never touched and the assertion passed while testing nothing.  The stub now
#   DIES (CLAUDE.md rule 12), so the statement fails honestly and the sweep's
#   p-load-with-recovery drops that one top-level form.  The row comes back for
#   real when #456 half (b) lands (hoist a sub an EARLIER section calls).
#   Same session, the opposite direction: perl-tests/sort.t's `ok(1, "SKIP:
#   stubborn AUTOLOAD ...")` was RESTORED to perl's own assertion (`sort
#   stubbedsub`), which passes now that the stub falls through to AUTOLOAD —
#   so the row COUNT of that pair is unchanged and only its honesty moved.
# s424 (#423, glob VALUE vs glob REF): substr.t 374 -> 375 EDITED BY HAND.
#   `my $x = *foo; is ref \$x, 'GLOB', '\substr does not coerce its glob arg just yet'`
#   (substr.t:784) — ref(\$x) answered REF (the box path treated every
#   typeglob-holding box as a glob ref); it answers GLOB now.  The only row that
#   moved in the s424 sweep (TOTAL 18364 -> 18365).
# s420 (#414, the hollow-token fix): postfixderef.t 94 -> 95 EDITED BY HAND.
#   The file's `package o` block registers a '.' overload whose body interpolates

#   went hollow between parse and emit), so the handler compiled to nil and
#   returned undef.  With the statement lowered, test 107 ("foo $s->$* bar does
#   concat overloading") passes and leaves fail-baseline.tsv by EDIT.  It is the
#   only row that moved in the whole sweep (per-file compare: every other file
#   byte-identical); TOTAL passing 18363 -> 18364.
# s399 (#323): assignwarn.t 116->96 and hashassign.t 309->305 EDITED BY HAND, not re-blessed —
#   the three t/test.pl warning helpers stopped manufacturing a pass, so 24 rows became honest
#   failures.  Cause for every one: PCL emits no warnings-gated diagnostic
#   (docs/not-supported.md section "Warnings-gated diagnostics are absent"; owner task #221).
# s405 (#346 harness half): ref.t 190 -> 191 EDITED BY HAND.  tools/pclperl-for-tests

# s408 (#363, an eval-mode DROP now DIES into $@): FIVE rows EDITED BY HAND.
#   dor.t 32->29, postfixderef.t 96->94, yadayada.t 21->20 — each lost row is a
#   '... compiles' assertion ($@ eq '') about code PCL genuinely cannot lower

#   eval.t 127->128 and magic.t 149->150 GAINED: eval.t because an invalid

#   `qq < … >` had been keeping its delimiters in the string value.
# s415 (#371, Option B phase 2 Track A): state.t 158 -> 0, status PARTIAL ->
#   TRANSPILE_FAIL, EDITED BY HAND.  The file's one `given (state $spam = $spam)`
#   block (line 350) is now a RULED REFUSAL rather than a silent drop --
#   given/when was removed in perl 5.42, so PCL refuses the file as perl does,
#   and a transpile-time refusal yields no TAP at all.  This trade was ruled
#   with Track A (docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md §2) and is not avoidable by
#   ordering: at the end of phase 2 EVERY remaining drop dies, and given/when
#   will still not be implemented.  Measured cost, both populations: this file
#   and t/op/state.t (126 rows) -- every other file the five refusal families
#   touch was already producing 0-27 rows.  Task #400 carries the trade and the
#   single condition that would reopen it.
# s415 (#370): bop.t 251 -> 253, EDITED BY HAND.  The two `is(~~$y, …)` rows
#   ran for the first time: PPI lexes a term-initial `~~` as the smart-match
#   operator, so both statements were DROPPED whole; the token repair
#   Parser2::_repair_term_initial_complement splits it into the two complements

# s418 (#343): bless.t 106/0->106/1 and split.t 184/9->178/6 EDITED BY HAND, not re-blessed —
